This satisfies REQ-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION. - validateStoryPath() parses the second token on the line as the storyPath and calls processStoryPath() with cwd, configured storyDirs, allowAbsolute, and requireExt. - processStoryPath(): - Calls performSecurityValidations() to handle absolute-path and traversal concerns (REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION) and short-circuits on failure. - If requireExt is true and hasValidExtension(storyPath) is false, reports messageId "invalidExtension" with the original path (extension enforcement and clear error message). - Calls reportExistenceProblems() to handle existence + boundary logic. - reportExistenceProblems(): - Uses normalizeStoryPath(storyPath, cwd, storyDirs) to build normalized candidates and get a status object. - Calls handleProjectBoundaryForExistence() to enforce that found or candidate paths remain within the project; if not, reports messageId "invalidPath" and returns (REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY). - If still valid, calls reportExistenceStatus() which: - For status "missing" → reports messageId "fileMissing" with the original path. - For status "fs-error" → reports messageId "fileAccessError" with the original path and a stringified error message (REQ-ERROR-HANDLING, clear UX diagnostics). - Rule meta.schema defines a single options object with properties: - storyDirectories: string[] - allowAbsolutePaths: boolean - requireStoryExtension: boolean This matches the configuration described in the story (REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS). - Error messages are descriptive: - fileMissing: "Story file '{{path}}' not found". - invalidExtension: "Invalid story file extension for '{{path}}', expected '.story.md'". - invalidPath: "Invalid story path '{{path}}'". - fileAccessError: "Could not validate story file '{{path}}' due to a filesystem error: {{error}}. Please check file existence and permissions.".
3) Path resolution, caching, filesystem and security utilities (REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION, REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE, REQ-PERFORMANCE-OPTIMIZATION, REQ-ERROR-HANDLING, REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY, REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION): - src/utils/storyReferenceUtils.ts - buildStoryCandidates(storyPath, cwd, storyDirs): - If storyPath starts with "./" or "../", returns [path.resolve(cwd, storyPath)]. - Else returns [path.resolve(cwd, storyPath), ...storyDirs.map(dir => path.resolve(cwd, dir, path.basename(storyPath)))]. This implements the story’s relative-from-project-root / storyDirectories behavior. - Caching and existence: - fileExistStatusCache: Map caches per absolute candidate. - checkSingleCandidate(candidate): - Returns cached result if present (REQ-PERFORMANCE-OPTIMIZATION). - Wraps fs.existsSync and fs.statSync in try/catch; never throws. - Distinguishes: - status "exists" (regular file), - "missing" (nonexistent or non-file), - "fs-error" (any filesystem exception, with error attached). - getStoryExistence(candidates): - Iterates candidates using checkSingleCandidate. - Returns status "exists" on first existing file with matchedPath. - Else, if any candidate had fs-error, returns status "fs-error" and the stored error. - Otherwise returns status "missing". - storyExists(paths) wraps getStoryExistence into boolean for backward compat. - __resetStoryExistenceCacheForTests() clears cache to avoid stale state across tests. - normalizeStoryPath(storyPath, cwd, storyDirs): - Uses buildStoryCandidates and getStoryExistence. - Returns { candidates, exists: existence.status === 'exists', existence } to expose full status for diagnostics. - enforceProjectBoundary(candidate, cwd): - Normalizes cwd and candidate with path.resolve and checks candidate === cwd or candidate startsWith(cwd + path.sep), returning {candidate, isWithinProject}. - Used by helpers to enforce REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY. - Security helpers: - isAbsolutePath(p) → path.isAbsolute(p). - containsPathTraversal(p): normalizes and checks for ".." segments. - isTraversalUnsafe(p): true if absolute or traversal. - hasValidExtension(p): path endsWith ".story.md". - isUnsafeStoryPath(p): isTraversalUnsafe or !hasValidExtension.
4) Project-boundary and security helpers (REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY, REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS): - src/rules/helpers/valid-story-reference-helpers.ts - analyzeCandidateBoundaries(candidates, cwd): - For each candidate, calls enforceProjectBoundary. - Aggregates hasInProjectCandidate/hasOutOfProjectCandidate. - handleProjectBoundaryForExistence(...): - If candidates exist: - If hasOutOfProjectCandidate && !hasInProjectCandidate, calls reportInvalidPath() and returns true (rejects entirely external candidates even if they exist). - If existenceResult.status === 'exists' and existenceResult.matchedPath is set: - Calls enforceProjectBoundary on matchedPath and, if outside project, reports invalidPath and returns true. - Otherwise returns false, allowing existence diagnostics to proceed. - performSecurityValidations(...): - Checks path.isAbsolute(storyPath). If absolute and allowAbsolute is false → reportInvalidPath and return false. - For potential traversal or directory separators, resolves normalized full path and if !full.startsWith(cwd + path.sep), reports invalidPath and returns false. - Returns true when it is safe to proceed.

traceability.notes:
The story 006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION requires an ESLint rule that validates @story file references end in .story.md, point to existing files within the project, enforce project boundaries and security constraints, handle filesystem errors gracefully, and support configurable story directories and path rules, with clear diagnostics and documentation.
The repo implements this via the valid-story-reference rule and supporting utilities. Path resolution uses context.cwd (falling back to process.cwd) and configurable storyDirectories, candidate paths are checked with cached, error-tolerant filesystem operations, project boundaries are enforced so that external files cannot be treated as valid even if they exist, and security concerns (absolute paths, traversal) are addressed. Diagnostics distinguish between missing files, invalid extensions, invalid paths, and filesystem access errors, and all messages include the offending path and, for fs errors, the underlying error message, satisfying both UX and error-handling acceptance criteria.
Tests in tests/rules/valid-story-reference.test.ts are explicitly tied to this story and exercise all major behaviors: core existence and extension checks, relative path resolution, path traversal and absolute path rejection, configuration options (storyDirectories, allowAbsolutePaths, requireStoryExtension), project boundary constraints (including misconfigured directories outside the project), and robust handling of EACCES/EIO-like filesystem failures with appropriate fileAccessError diagnostics. Documentation in docs/rules/valid-story-reference.md describes path resolution, project boundary rules, configuration, and examples exactly in line with the story’s Implementation Notes and examples.
Given the direct code, test, and documentation evidence, all acceptance criteria and listed requirements for 006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION are fully met, so the story is considered PASSED.
